title: Exploiting weight-space symmetries for approximating curvature
claim: Symmetry-induced group orbits yield equivariant gradient samples that can be summarized into a tractable approximation of an intractable Hessian.
layout: 2 stacked panels; top left-to-right network transform, bottom orbit-to-plot flow
description: The figure has two stacked parts. Top: two small neural-network diagrams, w in a gray rounded box on the left and a permuted w^(i) in a blue dashed box on the right. Hidden units are colored pink, orange and green and are swapped between the two. A black arrow labeled 'group action (leaving loss invariant)' joins them, and the weight matrices are labeled B, C and A^(i)B, CA^(i)T. Bottom: a schematic of parameter space, with axes at left and a dashed elliptical group orbit of light-blue points. The orbit contains an orbit average w*, and a gray arrow points to '(highly structured Hessian)'. A black-ringed point on the orbit is labeled {w, g}, with an arrow to 'intractable Hessian H'. Blue arrows run from the orbit to the set {w^(i), g^(i)} labeled 'gradient equivariance'. A black arrow leads from that set to a scatter plot of g^(i) against w^(i) with a red fit line. A red curved arrow points to 'tractable approximate Hessian Ĥ and Ĥ^-1'. Blue, gray and red text mark the stages.
caption: We present a framework for tractably approximating Hessians of large models by harnessing their inherent symmetries. Top: neural networks are typically invariant to many types of transformations, such as permutation of units within each layer (Sec. 2.1). Bottom: given a current parameter set w and associated loss gradient g, all similar pairs (w(i), g(i)) obtained by symmetry form the group orbit and are analytically accessible, as loss invariance implies gradient equivariance (Sec. 2.2). This large set describes how gradients vary across the parameter space. Here, we show that such curvature information can be implicitly manipulated and summarized into a tractable approximation ˆH to the intractable Hessian H (Sec. 3.1).
abstract: Many machine learning techniques rely on approximating a loss function's curvature, but this is notoriously hard to do at the scale of modern deep networks. Surprisingly, no previous work has exploited the curvature constraints that arise from well known weight-space symmetries in loss landscapes. By analytically averaging over group actions that leave the loss invariant, we construct structured Hessian approximations from single gradients that can be tractably estimated, stored, and inverted. The choice of user-specified symmetry group directly governs the trade-off between approximation accuracy and computational cost. Moreover, our framework provides a unifying theoretical lens for viewing existing methods; in particular, a specific choice of symmetry group recovers Shampoo/Muon-like curvature estimates. We validate our method on a range of network architectures, and deploy it to second-order optimization benchmarks, including a small language model. Our curvature estimation framework might find applications in other machine learning problems such as uncertainty estimation, continual learning, compression/pruning, training data attribution, and more.
